thumbnails.prompt_en: COMPOSITION RULE, HIGHEST PRIORITY: the photograph fills the entire 16:9 frame edge to edge — never a letterbox band, never an empty panel, never a flat colour block. The bottom three-eighths of the image height — that is the lowest 37%, roughly the bottom 270 pixels of a 720-pixel-tall frame — contains nothing but the bare dark polished table surface running toward the camera, dark and free of detail so overlay text stays readable on it. Every face, hand, photograph, telephone, folder and key object sits in the upper five-eighths. The table top runs across the MIDDLE of the frame, never near the bottom edge, and anything resting on it sits at mid height. Frame the man from the chest up and place his head high, close to the top edge. Scene: photographed from inside a dim Kremlin working office late at night, camera at standing eye level at the near end of a long walnut table. Vladimir Putin (President of Russia), in a dark navy suit and grey tie, sits on the right side of the frame, chest up, leaning over a spread of grey satellite prints that show road bridges with their centre spans dropped into the water. Behind him on the left a tall window looks out onto a floodlit courtyard, so the outside is bright and cold while the room around him stays dark under a single warm tungsten desk lamp, the two light sources meeting on his face. His face is pale and drained, lips pressed into a thin line, eyes narrowed and locked down on the prints, one flat hand pinning a photograph with whitened knuckles, a bead of sweat at the temple. Observed detail: one satellite print has curled at the corner and is held down by a desk telephone handset lying off its cradle, its cord tangled across the papers; Russian lettering in the map margins stays small and out of focus and legibility is not required. Style: candid documentary photograph of a real place, not an advertisement, not CGI, not a composite. Shot on a full-frame camera with a 35mm lens at about f/2.8, standing eye level, available light only, true-to-life restrained colour, mild sensor noise, a slight handheld tilt, honest texture on skin, wood, glass and metal. Signs may clip a little but the overall image stays natural — never glowing, never hyper-saturated, no HDR look, no rim-light effects, no lens flare.
